prerequisites.evidence: Prerequisite: CSC 415* (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the instructor.

other_requirements.evidence: Prerequisite: CSC 415* (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the instructor.

learning_outcomes: Describe how high level language programs are translated into machine language programs as well how machine language programs execute on CPU hardware (CSC 256, review).

Cultivate an understanding of the interface between hardware and software, with particular emphasis on modern Instruction Set Architectures (ISAs) and their relationship with datapath, control, and memory systems on computational platforms.
Develop an understanding of the factors contributing to the program performance and techniques for improving performance and apply them to sample problems.
Become familiar with the fundamentals of parallel processing on multi-core CPUs and many-core GPUs.
topics: Comparison with other ISAs: x86, ARM
Memories and caches and their impact on program performance
Shared-memory parallelism on CPUs and GPUs
Writing parallel codes and measuring their performance

skills.evidence: In this class we will focus on the MIPS ISA, which is a continuation of concepts from CSC 256
